## Research interests

I am interested in the theoretical foundations of reliable evaluation and reasoning about learned systems, particularly where hierarchical structure, statistical dependence, and limited data complicate inference. My current research develops and formally compares hierarchical Bayesian models of neural responses to naturalistic speech. This work has involved identifying failures of standard cross-validation assumptions in temporally structured data, redesigning evaluation procedures around conditionally independent units, and validating implementations against synthetic ground truth. I am interested in extending this methodological perspective to AI safety: understanding when evaluations of complex AI systems provide reliable evidence, how their statistical assumptions can be justified, and how formal analysis can reveal failures that conventional evaluation may miss.

## Research experience

04/2026 – now
:   **Master thesis: Cross-linguistic generalisation of the prosodic hierarchy**  
    Institute for the Interdisciplinary Study of Language Evolution (ISLE), University of Zürich. Prof. Dr. Martin Meyer (UZH) and Prof. Dr. Stefan Debener (Oldenburg), in collaboration with PD Dr. Elisa Pellegrino.  
    Asks whether the level-selective cortical entrainment pattern established for German by Oderbolz et al. (2024) — in which phase-amplitude coupling tracks a top-down structure from intonational phrase to foot to syllable — generalises to Italian, a typologically related but constraint-divergent language. Rather than a cross-linguistic comparison design, the study constructs a parallel Italian stimulus set following the same manipulation logic as the original paradigm and tests whether the same entrainment hierarchy emerges when both stimuli and listeners are Italian L1. Italian is a theoretically motivated test case because it shares core prosodic architecture with German (free lexical stress, a full prosodic hierarchy, focus encoded through prominence) but differs in constraint ranking: German prioritises rhythmic regularity, while Italian prioritises focus-driven phrasing. A difference in entrainment profiles would therefore implicate language-specific constraint ranking in shaping the quantitative expression of an otherwise shared hierarchical mechanism. The design is purely neural (EEG, ~30 Italian L1 listeners recruited in Zurich), with audio-motor synchronisation as a modular individual-differences predictor. Core analysis: pairwise phase consistency at theta, high delta, and low delta bands via glmertree, with PAC/DAR modelling as an extension.

06/2026 – now
:   **Research assistant**, LiRi Lab, University of Zürich  
    With Dr. Fivos Iliopoulos and Prof. Dr. Nathalie Giroud. 
    Assisting with hyperscanning EEG experiments investigating neural synchrony during social interaction, with responsibilities spanning experiment support and EEG preprocessing. 

06/2026 – now
:   **Hierarchical Bayesian TRF model comparison for speech encoding in iEEG**  
    Semester research project, Neural Dynamics Lab, Institute of Neuroinformatics, ETH Zürich. Prof. Dr. Timothée Proix, in collaboration with Prof. Dr. Balthasar Bickel (UZH & NCCR). 
    Designing and implementing a formal model comparison between two hierarchical Bayesian TRF frameworks for intracranial EEG: a raised-cosine basis-function model with patient/electrode random effects, and a hierarchical Gaussian Process model in which smoothness itself (kernel lengthscale and variance) is allowed to vary by patient, electrode, and word-level surprisal. Both are compared against standard ridge-regression mTRF via held-out predictive accuracy and WAIC/LOO across seven total model variants. Surprisal (GPT-2, word-level, extending to phoneme-level via recent phoneme-LM work) enters as a predictor of neural response to naturalistic speech (The Little Prince dataset), with an explicit focus on distinguishing gain-control from predictive-coding accounts of how prediction error reshapes the temporal response function. All code (Python: NumPy, SciPy, PyMC, MNE-Python) independently validated against synthetic ground truth at each stage before use on real data; to be released on the Neural Dynamics Lab GitLab.
    [More](../research/hierarchical-bayesian-trf.qmd)

06/2026 – now
:   **Adaptation of Vib2Sound for missing and degraded accelerometer cues**  
    Semester research project, Hahnloser Lab, ETH Zürich (supervisors: Mai Akahoshi and Yuhang Wang). 
    Extending Vib2Sound — a deep learning model for zebra finch vocalisation separation conditioned on body-mounted accelerometer signals — to handle cue degradation across a continuous spectrum rather than binary absence. The project implements and evaluates three complementary approaches: a cascade architecture guaranteeing the model never underperforms the audio-only baseline, continuous degradation training with realistic noise augmentation (Gaussian noise, gain reduction, band masking), and a Cross-Modal Correspondence contrastive loss to shape identity-discriminative audio representations without inference cost. Additional contribution to the BirdPark annotation pipeline.
    [More](../research/vib2sound-missing-cues.qmd)

## Computational projects

2025
:   **Homeric Formula Deviation Detector** (Python)  
    Information-theoretic signatures of narrative salience in oral poetry, using surprisal analysis over 15,683 lines of Ancient Greek. Parsed 15,683 lines of Ancient Greek, extracted 581 character mentions, computed -log₂(P(formula|context)) using n-gram models. High-surprisal moments (4.34-6.07 bits) clustered at narrative climaxes (deaths, armour exchanges), suggesting systematic exploitation of prediction error—parallel to efficient coding in sensory neuroscience.
    [Code](https://github.com/ellacapellini/homeric-formula-deviation)

2025
:   **Linear B Diachronic Phonological Mapper** (JavaScript, Python)  
    A toolkit for transcribing, parsing and visualising the phonological evolution of Mycenaean into Classical Greek. Handles syllabogram-to-phoneme mapping, morphological boundaries, frequency analysis of sign co-occurrence patterns.
    [Code](https://github.com/ellacapellini/Linear-B-Diachronic-Phonological-Mapper)
